: detached cabins and chalets on Sakwi Creek Road, Edelweiss Drive and Mt Downing Road, half-duplex product on Snowflake Crescent, and slope-side condo units on Enzian Way.

Tenure split today: UNVERIFIED: The OCP's build-out distribution proposes 40% public (nightly-rental) bed units, 45% private bed units and 15% resident/employee deed-restricted housing at full build-out — a plan target for the future resort, NOT a description of today's tenure split. No freehold/strata split for existing lots is stated.
Lot character: UNVERIFIED: No official source publishes a valley-wide lot-size or build-era profile; the OCP is a forward plan, not a stock survey.

Existing accommodation base, per the OCP: 226 resort residential units at Hemlock equating to 1,072 bed units, about 60% of them ski-in/ski-out or within comfortable walking distance of the base area. That is built resort stock, not vacant land.
Crown-land tenure nuance a land buyer must understand: inside the CRA, the resort developer uses Crown land under a licence of occupation for Resort Master Plan purposes.

Resort expansion vision, per the OCP and the provincially approved Resort Master Plan: a phased build-out toward 19,969 bed units and a Balanced Resort Capacity of 16,641 visitors per day, transforming the valley into a four-season resort community. This is a long-range plan vision longer than the life of the plan itself — NOT built product, NOT a subdivision, and NOT lots for sale.

The existing resort, for scale: 4 ski lifts servicing 146.8 hectares of developed ski terrain on 35 named trails, on the south and southwest slopes, using a 100% natural snowpack; Comfortable Carrying Capacity approximately 1,150 skiers/boarders per day, Balanced Resort Capacity 1,640 guests per day, per the OCP. Resort-operator claims beyond the OCP (lift status, current offerings, expansion timing) rest only on the operator's own marketing: UNVERIFIED here.
ALR vs non-ALR split: none stated

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Hemlock

items.t: "Hemlock" is a Fraser Valley Real Estate Board sub-area name, reported by SnapStats under the community Mission — it is not a municipality, and Hemlock Valley is not inside the City of Mission. Hemlock Valley is unincorporated land in FVRD Electoral Area C; the FVRD's Hemlock Valley Official Community Plan (November 2019) governs the plan area, and the FVRD administers that plan. (SnapStats FVR September 2026 report)

Plan-area basis: the OCP plan area is based on the Controlled Recreation Area (CRA) established by the Province in 2016 as part of approval of the Hemlock Valley All Seasons Resort Master Plan, for what is now Sasquatch Mountain Resort; the CRA carries the licence of occupation that lets the resort developer use Crown land for the purposes in the Resort Master Plan.

Mailing reality vs governance: live-page listings carry both "Mission, BC V0M 1A1" and "Agassiz, BC V0M 1A1" mailing addresses — neither mailing town is the governing authority; governance is FVRD Electoral Area C.

Neighbourhood planning areas inside the OCP area: Hemlock West (the historic resort community), Hemlock East and Hemlock North, each to be detailed through neighbourhood plans as the resort expands. Distances per the OCP: Agassiz (District of Kent) is approximately 38 km away, Mission approximately 55 km west, and the Village of Harrison Hot Springs sits at the southern end of Harrison Lake, south of the plan area.

Community scale: the FVRD's Hemlock Valley Evacuation Guide describes Hemlock Valley, a designated place in FVRD Area C, as having approximately 200 dwellings — mainly vacation homes and short-term rentals — with Sasquatch Mountain Resort at the village's upper end.

Schools — no school in the valley: the OCP states the small permanent population will limit the viability of locating schools and medical services within the CRA. Which district and school a Hemlock Valley address is catchment-assigned to: UNVERIFIED — no catchment document or locator run covers a valley address.
Per-sub-area medians are not published: UNVERIFIED. (SnapStats FVR September 2026 report)

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Hemlock

items.t: Governing plan — FVRD Hemlock Valley Official Community Plan (November 2019): The FVRD is responsible for administering the plan. Its chapters cover land use for Hemlock West / East / North, Infrastructure & Services (water supply, sanitary sewer, utilities and communications, stormwater, snow clearing and storage, solid waste, emergency/protective services), and Hazard & Risk Management including a Wildfire Interface Hazard section; Development Permit Areas in Schedule I include protection of development from hazardous conditions.
Servicing process: servicing is a resort-community system administered in the FVRD plan framework, not City of Mission services.

Hazard / DPA check before valuing a slope lot: the OCP's Development Permit Areas include hazardous-conditions protection and its risk chapter covers the wildfire interface — confirm the lot's DPA status with the FVRD. Parcel-level hazard status: UNVERIFIED.

Property taxes — RURAL regime (the only regime that applies here): a property not located in a city, town, district or village is in a rural area; its owner receives the tax notice from the Province's Surveyor of Taxes Office and pays the Province, not the FVRD. Under the Taxation (Rural Area) Act, s.11, rural taxes are due July 2, a 5% penalty is added to any portion unpaid on July 2, and a further 5% on any portion unpaid on October 31. Do not quote any city's tax dates for a Hemlock Valley lot.

Rental use: the FVRD describes the valley's dwellings as mainly vacation homes and short-term rentals, but any specific property's rental permission, strata rules and licensing still need parcel-level confirmation — the pattern is not a permission.

The mailing address lies in both directions: the same valley carries Mission V0M 1A1 and Agassiz V0M 1A1 mailing addresses, and neither town governs it — a buyer who calls Mission or Kent city hall about a Hemlock lot is calling the wrong government. Governance is FVRD Electoral Area C.

The valley has its own homeowners association, dating to 1980: the Hemlock Valley Homeowners Association, established in 1980, is a non-profit that works on behalf of valley homeowners — a community layer a lot buyer will not find in any listing.

Access is a single-road reality, on the FVRD's own evacuation planning: the FVRD evacuation guide's route for the valley runs past Sts'ailes First Nation and Harrison Mills — year-round living means outside services (no school, no medical service viable inside the CRA on the OCP's own analysis) and a ~38 km trip to Agassiz. The road's name, condition standard and winter maintenance responsibility on an official page: UNVERIFIED in the research.
No public transit to the valley was confirmed on an official source: UNVERIFIED — a lot purchase here is a car-dependent purchase on the sources checked.

faq.a: It is the current name of the Hemlock Valley ski area: the FVRD plan records 4 lifts, 146.8 hectares of developed ski terrain on 35 named trails and a single base lodge, on the south and southwest slopes of the mountain.

faq.q: How did Hemlock sell in September 2026?
faq.a: It did not record a sale in the permitted source: the sub-area showed 13 detached listings with 0 sold and 9 Condos & Townhomes listings with 0 sold, so no sales ratio or sub-area median exists for the month (as of September 2026, Source: SnapStats FVR September 2026 report).

faq.q: How many homes are for sale in Hemlock?
faq.a: At the end of September 2026 the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board figures showed 13 houses listed with 0 sold in the month and 9 condos and townhomes listed with 0 sold in the month in Hemlock. Those are month-end counts and move daily; ask Jared what is on the market today.

faq.q: Can Jared show me homes in Hemlock?
faq.a: Yes. Jared Gibbons, REALTOR® with Royal LePage Little Oak Realty, books private showings across the Fraser Valley and Metro Vancouver. Call or text 604-928-1361, or use the contact form on this site.

faq.q: Is Hemlock Valley part of Mission?
faq.a: No — SnapStats groups "Hemlock" under community Mission for reporting and many listings carry a Mission mailing address, but the valley is unincorporated FVRD Electoral Area C land governed by the FVRD's Hemlock Valley OCP. Title, permits and taxes run through the FVRD and the Province.

faq.q: Who provides water and sewer to a valley lot?
faq.a: A resort-community system administered in the FVRD plan framework — not City of Mission services. Which system a given lot is on, and its fees: UNVERIFIED — confirm with the FVRD for the parcel.

faq.q: Who do I pay property tax to, and when?
faq.a: The Province (Surveyor of Taxes), under the rural regime: due July 2, 5% on amounts unpaid July 2 and a further 5% on amounts unpaid October 31.

faq.q: Can I run a short-term rental on a valley lot/cabin?
faq.a: The valley's pattern is vacation homes and short-term rentals per the FVRD, but a specific property's rental permission, strata rules and licensing need parcel-level confirmation — and strata rental-restriction bylaws have been void since Nov 24, 2022 while short-term restrictions may still apply by bylaw.

faq.q: Where do children go to school if we live here full-time?
faq.a: There is no school in the valley — the OCP says the permanent population is too small to make one viable inside the CRA. The nearest Ministry-confirmed schools are in Agassiz (SD78) and at Deroche/Dewdney (SD75), but the catchment for a valley address is UNVERIFIED.
